batch.name: batch
batch.description: Long-running batch orchestration — a queue file of tasks; the engine admits the next lines into the window (wf-queue / queue_next: batch_size, after:, touches:, owner:, parked), each admitted task runs as a child session (`batch-task`: worktree → worker → merge + tests under the repo's land lock) driven by this agent, and every freed slot re-runs the pick; one fresh-eyes review of the combined diff.

plan_queue.prompt:
Build the task queue for this batch run.

0. **Handed over** — context `queue_file` already set = master's `enqueue_plan` queued the
   tasks of an approved plan (`queue_add`, window set): RESUME that queue (step 1's rules for
   `base:`; add `land_test:` / `record_file:` by hand once if the project has them), do not
   build a new one. Then go to step 3.
1. **Resume check** — list `{{context.cwd}}/.claude/batch/*.yaml`. If a
   queue file has pending or running tasks and matches the
   user's ask, RESUME it: `suspended` → `resume` the task sessions of
   the previous run (they keep their worktrees); a running task whose
   session is gone → `queue_mark({file, id, to: "released"})` (nothing
   of it landed) and its worktree is reused by the next pick. No
   `base:` entry → reconstruct it per repo (the last commit before the
   queue's first task landed: `git log --before=<queue file ctime>`).
   Then go to step 3.
2. **New queue** — create `{{context.cwd}}/.claude/batch/<short-name>.yaml`
   through `queue_add({queue: "<short-name>", task: {…}})` (the first add creates
   it), then `queue_header` for the window; header keys you write by hand once,
   before the run is live:
   ```yaml
   batch_size: 3
   reason: <why this window>
   base: [<repo-abs-path>=<sha>]
   land_test: <the project's test command, run after each merge; omit for none>
   record_file: <a file each landed task appends one record line to; omit for none>
   tasks:
     - id: T1
       status: pending
       difficulty: 7
       touches: [src/a, docs]
       text: |-
         <self-contained task prompt>
     - id: T2
       status: pending
       model: sonnet
       effort: high
       repo: other-repo
       after: [T1]
       touches: [src/b]
       text: |-
         <prompt>
   ```
   Keep the queue file out of git (untracked + ignored, e.g. `.claude/batch/`
   in `.gitignore`): a tracked queue dirties the tree on the first pick and
   every land refuses (exit 3).
   One `base:` entry per repo the tasks touch; <sha> = `git -C <repo>
   stash create` (snapshots a dirty tree without touching it) or `git -C
   <repo> rev-parse HEAD` when that prints nothing (clean tree).
   Task keys (`text` is the brief; `notes:` a list of `{from, date, text}`):
   - `difficulty:` — 1..10, how hard the task is: the task workflow's
     `model_table` maps it to the model/effort of each stage — worker,
     fix round, review, verifying review (see `batch-task`'s table) —
     and moves the worker and fix rows one row up on a second fix round. Prefer it to `model`/`effort`: the
     ledger keeps difficulty, model, effort and tokens per task, so the
     table can be tuned from data.
   - `kind:` — `bug`, `feature` or `research` (absent = feature): the
     task's type. The pick reports it; any other value is refused.
   - `model` / `effort` — a task without `difficulty:`, per
     task-delegation's table: opus/high for non-trivial
     code/judgement, sonnet/high for code from a detailed plan,
     sonnet/medium for routine review, haiku/low for runners.
     `model: —` = a task the parent does itself (never admitted).
   - `touches:` — the paths (prefixes) the task edits. Two tasks of one
     repo whose paths overlap never run together; a task WITHOUT
     `touches:` runs alone in its repo. With `overlap: files` in the
     header only FILE entries (an existing file, or a new path like
     `src/x/Foo.hx`) conflict, on the same file; a directory or glob
     entry is a hint. `owner:` — one
     name (`typer`, `typer.flow`): tasks of one owner run one at a
     time. `exclusive: true` — the task runs alone (mass moves, renames,
     reformats); while it waits for running lines of its repo, no later
     line of that repo is admitted (header `exclusive_hold: no` = off).
     `breaking: true` — a format or protocol change running processes
     cannot follow: admitted only into an empty window, nothing else
     admitted while it runs.
   - `after:` — ids that must be done first.
   - `repo:` — another repo (absolute path, or a name: the `base:` repo
     of that name, else the directory beside this project); default
     this project.
   - `workflow:` — the task's own task workflow (e.g. the heir of
     `batch-task` its repo defines); default this run's `task_workflow`.
   - `parked: true` — the task is skipped until unparked; `status: backlog`
     — kept for later, never picked (`queue_mark` `promoted` makes it pending).
   Each task runs in its OWN worktree (`<repo>/../.wt/<repo-name>/<ID>`,
   branch `batch/<ID>`) and lands by `git merge --no-ff` + `land_test`,
   one land per repo at a time — so tasks need not avoid sharing
   infrastructure files; `touches:` is about logic that must not be
   edited twice at once. Each task is self-contained: a worker sees ONLY
   its task. `batch_size` = max parallel tasks; `batch_size: 0` (with its
   `reason:`) pauses: running tasks finish, nothing new starts. The user may
   edit the file mid-run — every pick re-reads it.
3. `context_set(key: "queue_file", value: "<absolute path>")` (the project's
   `.claude/batch/<name>.yaml` written out as an absolute path: task sessions get the
   path and never re-resolve a name from their own repo) and
   `context_set(key: "task_workflow", value: "batch-task")` (a project
   with its own heir of `batch-task` names it here).
Optional: `context_set(key: "memory_index", value: "<absolute path>")` — the project's memory index
file; task drivers hand it to their decider (skip it when the project has none).
4. → transition `ready`.

Statuses: pending, running, done, failed, backlog. Only the
engine changes them: `queue_next` / `queue_mark` (exec: `wf-queue`),
under the queue's lock. Once the run is live, change the queue through
the same lock: `queue_add` (a new task, checked as a pick reads it),
`queue_edit` (a task's fields, a note), `queue_header` (window / pause
with its reason), `queue_mark` with `retry: true` (a failed task again;
its `difficulty:` goes up by one, so the re-run starts a model row up)
— a script or sed edit can drop a status an exec writes at that moment. The queue FILE is the source of truth — it
survives context compression and session restarts.
plan_queue.task: Build or resume the batch queue

paused.prompt:
The queue is paused (`batch_size: 0`) and none of its tasks runs:
{{stderr}}
Tell the user the pause and its reason (the comment above). When they lift it (`queue_header({file:
"{{context.queue_file}}", batch_size: N, reason})`, or their own edit) → `retry`; to end the run now → `report`.

dispatch.prompt:
The pick admitted (and set running in {{context.queue_file}}) one line per free slot, `ID model effort repo workflow difficulty kind` (`kind` is `feature` when the line has none):
{{stdout}}
{{stderr}}

For EACH admitted line, one task session:
1. `start({workflow: <its workflow column; `-` → "{{context.task_workflow}}">, parent_session_id:
   "{{session_id}}", cwd: "<its repo>", context: {task: "<ID>", queue_file: "{{context.queue_file}}",
   difficulty: "<its difficulty column>"}}; add `memory_index: "{{context.memory_index}}"` to
   that context when it is not empty)` — for a line whose difficulty is `-` pass instead
   `model: "<its model column>", effort: "<its effort column>"` (a `-` column: leave that key out) → session P (the repo's own
   workflows are found from that cwd).
2. A task workflow with a `driver:` (bundled `batch-task`) — `start`'s answer ends with a DRIVER block:
   spawn exactly that Agent call (copy it, change nothing), then `link_agent({session_id: P, agent_id:
   <its id>})`. Do NOT drive P yourself: the driver runs its prompts and answers with one line.
   Without a DRIVER block, drive P by its prompts yourself, passing session_id P in every call.
3. context_set `tasks` on THIS session ({{session_id}}): one `ID=P driver=<agent id or ->` per running
   task session (all of them, not only the new ones) — after a context compression
   `status({session_id: "{{session_id}}", key: "tasks"})` and `sessions` are the truth, not your memory.
Then transition `dispatched` and END your turn: agent notifications wake you in `collect`.

collect.prompt:
Task sessions: `status({session_id: "{{session_id}}", key: "tasks"})` (ID=P). Last pick: {{stderr}} Woken by a DRIVER's one line (the task's bookkeeping — done, the record line — is already done): - `LANDED task= …` / `CLOSED task= …` → the task session ended: route below. Their `lessons=; …|none` tail is the agents' own follow-ups, copied: turn each into a `queue_add` line, a memory note, or nothing. A trailing `decided=` means a decider answered design choices without you: audit that file (`## ` / `decision:` / `why:` blocks) and overrule a wrong one with a `queue_add` line. - `NEEDS-PARENT task= session=

reason=… see=` → read only the named file. A design choice or a decision the prompt left open → SendMessage the driver your decision and tell it to continue; a rejected or blocked task → SendMessage the driver its exact path: from `review` transition `reject`, from `work` `blocked`, from `land_failed` `close` (each leads to `blocked`); then in `blocked` `queue_mark` to `failed` with note "" and transition `close` (`stop` only when you say so). Then decide whether to `queue_add` a follow-up line; anything that needs the user → tell the user, keep the slot. Never take over the task's work. - a worker or reviewer whose spawner is a driver → its driver handles it: ignore it while the driver runs. After a restart the line may reach you instead: relay it by SendMessage to the driver linked to P. Only when that SendMessage fails (the driver is gone), re-spawn from `driver_call` and send the line to the new driver; a driver that stays silent is the stale sweep's (below). Never both, never drop it. A task session you drive yourself (no driver): find it (the agent is linked to a session whose parent is P; `sessions` shows `[agent …]`), read `status(P)` and advance P by its prompt (session_id P). A transition into P's exec steps (the land waits for the repo's land lock) may outlive the call and finish in the background — move other tasks meanwhile. Resumed after a restart: every task session P is YOURS — `resume` each; the sessions the resume lists are their agents' (SendMessage exactly as it prints). A driven P whose driver is gone → re-spawn it: `status({session_id: P, key: "driver_call"})` is the exact Agent call `start` gave (it continues from `status`: the session holds the step), then `link_agent` it and update `tasks`. Stale sessions of this run — no engine call past their state's `stale_after` (`status({session_id: "{{session_id}}"})` lists them anew): {{stale_sessions}} A stale session with an agent → SendMessage that agent asking where it stands; no answer, or the agent is gone → spawn a fresh agent on the SAME session with the first one's prompt (it continues from `status`: the session holds the step) and `link_agent` it — for a driver that prompt is `status({session_id: P, key: "driver_call"})`. A stale task session P without an agent is yours: `status(P)` and advance it. Route this session: - a task session reached its terminal (`done` / `closed` / `released`) → update `tasks`, then `slot_free` (the pick runs again and refills the freed slot). - a task session ended `stopped` → `stop`. - task sessions still running, none ended → END your turn here, no transition. - none of YOURS runs and the last pick admitted nothing (exit 10: the running tasks left belong to other sessions, or block by overlap) → `stalled`.

cross_check.prompt:
All workers finished. A `batch-task` reviewed each task alone
before its land; this is the run's fresh-eyes review of the WHOLE
(a task workflow without its own review — a project heir — gets
its only review here). Workers do NOT review themselves (a
sub-agent's coding/bug-fix review stops at lint + its own intent
re-read — the spawner owns the independent review).

1. The run's diff, per `base:` repo: `git -C <repo> diff <sha> --stat`
   (a `review_base:` line from a previous visit → diff from it
   instead: this visit reviews only the refill's delta) — it covers
   merged worktree branches and uncommitted shared-tree edits alike;
   plus `git -C <repo> ls-files --others --exclude-standard` — new
   files a shared-tree worker never committed are NOT in the diff.
   Compare both against the task lines in {{context.queue_file}}.
2. Batch the changed files for review like code-review does:
   source+test together, change-coupled files together, then by
   directory; at most 5 files AND ~500 changed lines per batch;
   under ~40 changed lines of purely mechanical/wiring diffs → no
   agent, review those lines yourself in step 3. Each batch agent
   gets its file list, `git -C <repo> diff <sha> -- <file>` per file
   (a new file: read it whole), scope `diff`, "report one section per
   file + a batch-level cross-file section", explicit `model` and `effort`
   (sonnet/medium for linter-covered/routine code, opus/high for
   engine-critical / concurrency / no-linter), and this preamble
   VERBATIM:
---
IMPORTANT: Override the default CLAUDE.md rule about start().
Do NOT call start() without arguments.
Instead, your FIRST action must be:
  mcp__plugin_workflow_wf__start({ workflow: "file-review", parent_session_id: "<SESSION_ID>" })
where <SESSION_ID> is the current session ID (substitute it before sending).
Then follow the file-review workflow states until completion.
start() returns `SESSION: <id>` — pass that session_id explicitly in every
subsequent workflow tool call; parallel siblings share the same ppid.
---
   Up to 8 agents in ONE message, each `run_in_background: false`;
   more batches → next wave. `sessions` → `abort` their orphaned
   child sessions after collecting.
3. The agent-less lines from step 2, then cross-task seams on top
   of the batch reports: two tasks touched
   the same file (the "independent" assumption was violated),
   duplicated code introduced by different workers, conflicting
   assumptions.
4. Real findings: trivial → fix inline; substantial → first write
   one `review_base: <repo-abs-path>=<sha>` header key per repo (same
   snapshot rule as `base:`, taken NOW) into the header, then append the findings as
   new pending tasks (`queue_add`) and → `refill` (the pick admits them like any
   other line). At most 3 visits — on the 3rd (the
   engine's `Revisit #3` header) no `refill`: fix inline or list what
   remains for the report as a human decision (a 4th entry throws).
5. No findings → `done`.

report.prompt:
The queue is drained. Final pass:
1. `sessions` → `abort` any remaining orphaned child sessions.
2. Read {{context.queue_file}} and write the summary the user
   will actually read:
   - What the batch ACCOMPLISHED — outcomes grouped by theme,
     not a per-task echo of the queue.
   - Counts: done / failed / total; one line per failed task with
     its reason; why the remaining pending tasks were not admitted
     (the last pick's reasons: after:, parked, overlap, pause).
   - Review verdict (findings and how they were resolved, seams
     between tasks, or "clean").
   - Anything left unverified or needing a human decision.
→ `done`.

batch-task.name: batch-task
batch-task.description: One task of a `batch` queue — a child session a cheap DRIVER agent runs for the batch dispatcher (`driver:`): claim (the line's difficulty → model/effort by model_table) → project_prepare [exec: a worktree beside the repo] → work (one worker agent) → work_check [exec: one clean commit on the branch] → review_scope [exec: the diff's class → the reviewer's model] → review (one reviewer agent; FIXES → work) → project_land [exec: merge --no-ff + the queue's land_test under the repo's land lock] → mark_done [exec: `[x]` + the record_file line] → cleanup [exec] → done. A project overrides project_prepare / project_land through `extends: batch-task`.

claim.prompt:
Task session {{session_id}} (dispatcher {{parent_session_id}}), repo {{context.cwd}}. The pick already
set the task running. Every `transition` reply IS the next prompt — never call `status` after it.
context_set on THIS session (session_id {{session_id}}), each its own call — skip a key the dispatcher
already passed to `start` (task {{context.task}}, queue_file {{context.queue_file}}, difficulty
{{context.difficulty}}; empty = not passed; model and effort are in `status`, not printed here — a
driven task needs none of the queue line):
  task       — the line's ID
  queue_file — the queue's absolute path (the dispatcher's `queue_file`)
  memory_index — the project's memory index path, when the dispatcher has one ({{context.memory_index}}; optional)
  difficulty — the line's difficulty column, when it is not `-`: the engine then sets `model` and
               `effort` from this workflow's model_table (its reply names them) — do not set them yourself
  model, effort — ONLY when the line has no difficulty: its columns (effort `-` → task-delegation's table)
Then transition `prepare` (an exec: the worktree is made before any agent starts).

project_prepare.command:
case "$TASK" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) echo "refused task id: '$TASK'" >&2; exit 2;; esac
repo=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) || exit 2
root=$(dirname "$repo")/.wt/$(basename "$repo")
wt=$root/$TASK
if [ -d "$wt" ]; then
  echo "kept $wt ($(git -C "$wt" symbolic-ref --short HEAD) @ $(git -C "$wt" rev-parse --short HEAD))" >&2
else
  mkdir -p "$root" || exit 1
  git worktree add "$wt" -b "batch/$TASK" HEAD >&2 || exit 1
  echo "made $wt on batch/$TASK @ $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" >&2
fi
printf %s "$wt"

prepare_failed.prompt:
The worktree for {{context.task}} was not made (exit {{exit_code}}):
{{stderr}}
A stale branch `batch/{{context.task}}` without its directory: decide (delete it only if it holds nothing
unmerged) and `retry`. Otherwise `queue_mark({file: "{{context.queue_file}}", id: "{{context.task}}", to:
"released"})` (back to pending, nothing was made) → `release`, or `to: "failed"` with the reason as `note`
→ `close`.

work.prompt:
{{stderr}}
Worktree {{context.wt}} (branch `batch/{{context.task}}`). Visit {{visits.work}} of 3.
First visit — start the worker's session yourself, then hand it to the agent:
1. `start({workflow: "subagent", parent_session_id: "{{session_id}}", cwd: "{{context.wt}}"})` → W;
   context_set `worker_session` = W.
2. Spawn ONE worker: Agent, model {{context.model}}, effort {{context.effort}}, `run_in_background: true`;
   context_set `worker_model` = "{{context.model}}/{{context.effort}}". Prompt:

     You are the worker of task {{context.task}}. Your brief is its entry in {{context.queue_file}}
     (read it there; it is self-contained). Your workflow session is W, already started — do NOT call
     start(): first `status({session_id: "W"})`, then follow it to its terminal, passing session_id W
     in every call; every `transition` reply IS the next prompt — never call `status` after it. Work
     ONLY inside {{context.wt}} (branch `batch/{{context.task}}`): ONE commit on that branch, a clean
     worktree at the end; never touch {{context.cwd}} itself; never push. Check the on-disk state
     first — work already applied is reconciled, not done twice. Your report is a FILE: write
     {{context.wt}}.log/report.md (what changed and why, the checks run; then the sections
     `## Follow-up not done`, `## Tool defect found`, `## Open` — each a short list, `none` when empty;
     mkdir -p the dir), and {{context.wt}}.log/handoff.md when you stop unfinished (the same three sections). On a fix
     round, carry the previous report.md's three sections' items into the new file. Answer with ONE line:
     `DONE <sha> report={{context.wt}}.log/report.md` or `BLOCKED <reason> report=<the file>`.
     Every background task you started (a Bash `run_in_background`, a Monitor, an Agent) is stopped
     (TaskStop) or awaited before your one line: never end your turn with live background work, the
     driver's notification fires only when you stop with none. Every wait loop you write (`until … do sleep …; done`) also
     ends on failure: the watched job's exit, a FAILED / refused marker, or a timeout — never on the
     success marker alone.

3. `link_agent({session_id: W, agent_id: <its id>})` (the engine records it as this visit's agent);
   context_set `worker_agent` = its id.
A later visit (a fix round, the cause from the review or the land) arrives as "Revisit #N", and the
values this prompt rendered are the first visit's: read each one it uses from P's context now
(`status` with `key`) — `model_fix` / `effort_fix` (a fix round's worker; empty — no difficulty, or a
table without a `fix` stage — = `model` / `effort`) against `worker_model` (stored as `model/effort`), and `worker_agent`, `worker_session`:
- the same `model/effort` → SendMessage `worker_agent` with the cause: its one line plus "read <its file>
  whole" (never the file's text pasted); then `link_agent({session_id: <worker_session>, agent_id:
  <worker_agent>})` again — it marks the worker as this visit's;
- different model or effort (the fix stage's row, or an escalation, names another) → steps 1–3 again with `model_fix` /
  `effort_fix` (empty = `model` / `effort`) in place of `model` / `effort`: a fresh worker on the new model, its
  prompt above plus "a fix round of a previous worker's branch: <the cause's line> — read <its file> whole".
Then END your turn on this task. On the worker's notification: context_set `tokens_worker` = the
value already set ({{context.tokens_worker}}, empty = 0) PLUS this agent's tokens from its notification's
usage line. Then transition `check`: the engine verifies the tree (artifacts outrank the report) in the
next step; the worker is stuck, or the work is wrong and another round would not help → `blocked`.

work_check.command:
branch=batch/$TASK
n=$(git log --oneline "HEAD..$branch" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
dirty=$(git -C "$WT" status --porcelain)
echo "commits on $branch beyond HEAD: $n"; git log --oneline "HEAD..$branch" 2>/dev/null | head -5
[ -z "$dirty" ] || { echo "worktree $WT not clean:"; echo "$dirty" | head -10; }
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$dirty" ]

review.prompt:
{{stderr}}
Review {{visits.review}} of 3 of {{context.task}} (branch `batch/{{context.task}}`, worktree {{context.wt}}).
1. Spawn ONE reviewer: Agent, `subagent_type: "workflow:reviewer"` (the read-only type: no workflow tools,
   so it has no session of its own), model {{context.review_model}}, effort {{context.review_effort}} (both
   empty → {{context.model}}, {{context.effort}}); from review 2 on (a verification of the fixes)
   model {{context.model_review_verify}}, effort {{context.effort_review_verify}} instead (empty =
   keep the above); `run_in_background: true`, prompt:

     You review task {{context.task}} of {{context.queue_file}}, read-only: its line is the brief, the
     change is `git -C {{context.cwd}} diff HEAD...batch/{{context.task}}`; the change's working tree is
     {{context.wt}}: read the sources there. You have no workflow session: call no workflow tool. Your review is a
     FILE: write, with the Write tool, /tmp/wf-batch-logs/{{context.task}}/review.md (the verdict, the reasons; for FIXES the full fix list;
     a section `## Notes (non-blocking)` with the follow-ups you saw, `none` when empty; when review.md already exists (an earlier round), carry its `## Notes (non-blocking)` items into the new file; the Write tool creates the dir). Your LAST step is ONE SubagentHandback call with ONE line: `VERDICT MERGE|FIXES|REJECT <one-line summary>
     review=/tmp/wf-batch-logs/{{context.task}}/review.md design=yes|no` (design=yes: a fix needs a design choice).
     Every background task you started (Bash `run_in_background`, Monitor, Agent) is stopped or awaited
     before that handback: never end your turn with live background work. End every wait loop on the
     watched job's exit, a FAILED marker or a timeout, never on the success marker alone.

2. END your turn on this task (the reviewer has no session to `link_agent` to).
On its notification: context_set `tokens_review` = the value already set ({{context.tokens_review}},
empty = 0) PLUS this agent's tokens, then route by the verdict: MERGE → `land`; FIXES → `fix` (the
worker's cause = the verdict line + "read /tmp/wf-batch-logs/{{context.task}}/review.md whole"; with design=yes the driver first asks its decider, see its instructions, and adds "read {{context.wt}}.log/decisions.md whole"); REJECT → `reject`. The context_set first, the transition after
it returned.

project_land.command:
case "$TASK" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) echo "refused task id: '$TASK'"; exit 2;; esac
branch=batch/$TASK
state() { echo "repo state:"; git log --oneline -3; git status --short --untracked-files=no | head -10; }
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then
  echo "refused: $(pwd) has uncommitted changes"; git status --short --untracked-files=no | head -5; exit 3
fi
test_cmd=$("$WF_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/wf-queue" "$QUEUE" --header land_test) || exit 2
before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
if ! out=$(git merge --no-ff --no-edit "$branch" 2>&1); then
  echo "$out" | tail -20; git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | head -20
  git merge --abort 2>/dev/null || git reset -q --keep "$before" ||
    { echo "merge of $branch failed and could not be taken back"; state; exit 4; }
  echo "merge of $branch onto $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) failed: taken back"; exit 1
fi
merged=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
if [ -n "$test_cmd" ]; then
  log=$(mktemp); sh -c "$test_cmd" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    tail -40 "$log"; rm -f "$log"
    # Only the merge is taken back: --keep refuses to touch a file edited meanwhile, and a HEAD that
    # moved during the test (a commit, another branch) is never reset.
    [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$merged" ] || { echo "HEAD moved during land_test: nothing taken back"; state; exit 4; }
    git reset -q --keep "$before" ||
      { echo "local edits on files the merge changed: the merge is left on top"; state; exit 4; }
    echo "land_test failed (exit $rc): the merge of $branch is taken back"; exit 1
  fi
  tail -5 "$log"; rm -f "$log"
fi
echo "landed $branch: $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

land_timeout.command:
echo "repo state:"; git log --oneline -3; git status --short --untracked-files=no | head -10
! git merge-base --is-ancestor "batch/$TASK" HEAD && [ -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]

land_failed.prompt:
The land of {{context.task}} failed (exit {{exit_code}}):
{{stdout}}
{{stderr}}
- 3 (the repo's own tree has uncommitted changes) → never stash or reset someone's work: tell the
  user and `retry` once it is clean, or `stop`.
- 1 (merge conflict, or land_test failed — the merge is taken back) → `fix`: the cause goes to the
  worker as its fix round; `close` when it cannot be fixed in the branch.
- 4 (the merge could not be taken back safely: HEAD moved during land_test, or local edits on the

mark_done.command:
sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) || exit 1
"$WF_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/wf-queue" "$QUEUE" --done "$TASK" --note "landed $sha" || exit 1
rec=$("$WF_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/wf-queue" "$QUEUE" --header record_file) || exit 1
[ -n "$rec" ] || exit 0
case "$rec" in /*) ;; *) rec=$(dirname "$QUEUE")/$rec;; esac
printf '%s\n' "- $(date +%Y-%m-%d) $TASK landed $sha | difficulty: ${DIFFICULTY:--} | model: $MODEL/$EFFORT | review: ${REVIEW_MODEL:-$MODEL}/${REVIEW_EFFORT:-$EFFORT} | rounds: $ROUNDS | tokens: worker=${TOKENS_WORKER:-0} review=${TOKENS_REVIEW:-0} | report: $WT.log/report.md" >>"$rec" ||
  { echo "warning: the record line for $TASK was not appended to $rec" >&2; exit 0; }
echo "recorded $TASK in $rec"

cleanup.command:
case "$TASK" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) echo "refused task id: '$TASK'"; exit 2;; esac
case "$WT" in /*/"$TASK") ;; *) echo "refused worktree path: '$WT'"; exit 2;; esac
if [ -d "$WT" ]; then
  dirty=$(git -C "$WT" status --porcelain)
  [ -z "$dirty" ] || { echo "kept $WT: not clean"; echo "$dirty" | head -5; exit 1; }
  git worktree remove --force "$WT" || exit 1
fi
git branch -d "batch/$TASK" || exit 1
echo "removed $WT and batch/$TASK"

that batch agent's cross-file section — do not re-derive them; focus
on seams BETWEEN batches and on set-wide patterns (these apply even
when there was only one batch):
- [ ] Duplication across files
- [ ] Missing updates to consumers of changed interfaces
- [ ] Consistency across files
- [ ] Integration between changed components
- [ ] Agent-less batches: lines the mass gate kept without a reviewer

(a dangling object: no branch or ref changes, nothing enters history;

reworked logic — is done INLINE by the orchestrator, top-tier
included (a delegated nit round pays a full agent's fixed cost for
trivial work). Delegate only when the fix set introduces or reworks
logic; then prefer resuming the ORIGINAL implementer (SendMessage)
over a fresh agent — its context is already paid for.

overview.prompt:
Do these steps in order, then transition `understood`:

**Step 1 — Determine file source (first match wins):**

1. **User specified files** — user named concrete file paths → use those.
   Do NOT touch git.
2. **User specified directories** — user named directories or patterns
   (e.g. "src/api/", "src/ without editor", "src/*.hx, src/api/, src/drill/").
   Parse the request in natural language:
   - `"src/"` → all source files recursively, auto-group by first-level subdirectories
   - `"src/api/, src/drill/"` → only these dirs recursively, each = one package
   - `"src/*.hx, src/api/, src/drill/"` → root files + specific dirs
   - `"src/ without editor and video"` → everything except excluded dirs
   Use Glob to build the final file list. Group files by parent directory into packages.
   Save via `context_set(key: "review_mode", value: "directory")`.
   Save via `context_set(key: "packages", value: "<JSON array>")` where format is:
   `[{"name": "api", "files": ["src/api/Foo.hx", ...]}, {"name": "root", "files": [...]}]`
   Save via `context_set(key: "current_package_index", value: "0")`.
3. **Called as sub-workflow after testing/coding** — you already know which files
   were changed from conversation history. Use that knowledge directly.
4. **Starting fresh with no prior context** — check git status for uncommitted
   changes (staged or unstaged). If none → ask the user.
- NEVER default to `git diff master` or full branch diff

**Step 2 — Determine review depth:**
- Coming from testing/coding / "check changes" / "review diff" / default
  → `scope: diff` (only review changed lines)
- "review file" / "check whole file" / "bring to order" (or equivalent
  phrases in the user's language) → `scope: full` (review entire file)
- Directory mode → always `scope: full`
Save the scope via `context_set(key: "review_scope", value: "diff" or "full")`.

**Step 3 — Get file names:**
- If source is user-specified files or directories → already have the list.
- If source is git → get ALL changed file names (modified AND new/untracked):
  - Modified/staged: `git diff HEAD --name-only --diff-filter=d`
    (lowercase `d` excludes deleted files)
  - New untracked: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`
  Combine both lists. Do NOT read full diffs yet — names only.
  Deleted files (`git diff HEAD --name-only --diff-filter=D`) get NO
  per-file review — note them for the cross-file step instead
  (their callers/imports may break).
  **Git pathspec gotcha (zsh):** to exclude paths, use `-- . ':(exclude)path'`,
  NOT `-- ':!path'` — the latter silently returns empty results in zsh.

Output the file list (and packages if directory mode), then → transition `understood`.

1. Typos, edge cases, off-by-one, null refs
2. Does the change affect surrounding logic?
3. Ripple check — grep all call sites of changed functions

- `fix` → go back and fix

1. New + old code together — do they fit?
2. Dead code — did the fix make something unnecessary?
3. Constants/config — magic values?
4. Simplification opportunities?
- `ok` → done
- `fix` → needs more work

write.prompt:
Text-only change: every file touched is prose that no compiler or linter
checks (skill SKILL.md, workflow YAML, CLAUDE.md, memory files, reports,
plans, README prose). If ANY touched file is code or tool config
(settings.json, .mcp.json, package.json…) → transition `not_docs` (the
parent re-routes to coding). A NEW bundled workflow also needs its name in
`Engine.GLOBAL_WORKFLOWS` (src/engine.ts) — that is code → `not_docs`.

1. Set `context_set("doc_kind", <kind>)` to the STRICTEST kind present:
   - `workflow` — a workflow YAML (templates/, ~/.claude/workflows/,
     .claude/workflows/). Load `Skill("workflow-authoring")` first if it
     is not loaded.
   - `knowledge` — SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, memory: durable instructions every
     future session obeys. Every rule you write must be sourced from THIS
     session (a command output, a user statement, a file you read) — never
     from how a tool "usually" behaves. Prefer recording the convention over
     recording a defect.
   - `note` — reports, plans, scratch notes, README prose.
2. See the original before changing: `git show HEAD:<file>` (tracked) or the
   file itself. Edit within the requested scope — no rewrites of accurate
   neighbouring text.

→ `verify`

verify.prompt:
Re-read the diff ONCE against the request — the one check no tool runs.
Then the kind-specific check (`doc_kind` = {{context.doc_kind}}):
- `workflow` →
  - a BUNDLED template (the plugin's `templates/`): make sure the edit sits
    in the dir the RUNNING server loads from (`ps -axo command | grep
    build/index.js` shows the path — a plugin cache copy may be dead
    weight), then trigger the reload per workflow-authoring;
  - a user/project workflow (`~/.claude/workflows/`, `.claude/workflows/`):
    those dirs are fs.watch'ed — no trigger needed.
  Then confirm with `list` that the workflow is present with the expected
  state count: a file with a YAML error (duplicate key, unknown
  `transitions`/`cases`/`default`/`on_success`/`on_error` target) is
  skipped silently and vanishes from it. `list` does NOT catch a bad
  `on_complete`/`on_fail` target or an unknown `sub_workflow` name —
  check every one you added or renamed by hand. `npm test` does not
  validate your file either (a malformed template is skipped there too).
- `knowledge` → for each factual claim you added, name its in-session
  evidence; a claim without evidence is removed or marked unverified.
- `note` → nothing further.

No reviewer agent, no lint, no tests: fresh eyes pay off on logic the author
is blind to, not on a paragraph the author already sees whole.

→ `done` when the edit matches the request; `fix` when the re-read found it
wrong (back to write).

explore.name: explore
explore.description: Codebase exploration workflow — understand structure, trace code, find patterns

scope.prompt:
Determine what we're looking for and where.

Exploration types:
- **Structure** — project layout, module boundaries, dependency graph
- **Feature** — how a specific feature is implemented end-to-end
- **Pattern** — recurring code patterns, conventions, idioms
- **Code path** — trace execution flow through the codebase

1. Check loaded skills, MEMORY.md, and project CLAUDE.md first
2. If the answer is already available → transition `already_known`
3. If exploration is needed → transition `explore`

investigate.prompt:
Explore the codebase using available tools.

**Preferred approach:**
- Launch parallel subagents for independent questions. Location-only
  fan-out (find files/symbols, paste back what's there, zero judgement)
  may use flat `Explore`-type agents; any agent that returns judgement,
  analysis, or a recommendation is ANALYTICAL — never spawn it flat,
  use the VERBATIM preamble below. ALWAYS pass an explicit `model`:
  `haiku` (effort low) for locate fan-out that returns places only,
  `opus` (effort high) for analytical judgement; fable only on user
  request, never silent session-model inheritance. Their
  findings gate your next transition → ALL calls in ONE message,
  each with `run_in_background: false` (a single spawn especially —
  never background one gating agent).
- Use Glob to find files by pattern
- For "where is X / what is X's shape / which decls carry Y" use the
  STRUCTURAL navigation tool your loaded skills prescribe for the
  language (a parser-aware query CLI, LSP, etc.) — NOT grep — when
  one exists. Grep/Read only for non-parsing files or prose inside
  comments/strings. The loaded coding skills are authoritative here;
  follow the tool-usage gate defined by the loaded skills, do not
  default to grep.

**Reading budget** (tool-agnostic — the loaded skills map it onto the tool):
- Read the NODE a hit pointed at, never the file: `file:line` buys that
  member or that range, not the whole file.
- A walker's scope is the narrowest directory the previous hit named;
  the whole tree is for the FIRST query only.
- A file no hit named stays closed. "Just in case" is where whole-file
  reads come from.

**Rules:**
- Locate with the structural tool first, then narrow with Read
- Follow imports and call chains to understand flow
- Note key files, patterns, and architectural decisions

For an ANALYTICAL subagent, include in its prompt VERBATIM:
---
IMPORTANT: Override the default CLAUDE.md rule about start().
Do NOT call start() without arguments.
Instead, your FIRST action must be:
  mcp__plugin_workflow_wf__start({ workflow: "subagent", parent_session_id: "<SESSION_ID>" })
where <SESSION_ID> is the current session ID (substitute it before sending).
Then follow the subagent workflow until completion — its `route` state
self-classifies (analytical → skill-loaded sub-workflow; trivial → execute).
start() returns `SESSION: <id>` — pass that session_id explicitly in every
subsequent workflow tool call; parallel siblings share the same ppid.
---
After collecting reports: `sessions` → `abort` orphaned child `subagent`
sessions.

Budget: 4 visits to this state (engine-enforced); when nearly exhausted,
choose `not_found` instead of retrying.

Choose transition:
- `found` → gathered enough information to answer
- `deeper` → need to explore further (follow a lead, check another area)
- `ask_user` → need user input to decide direction (e.g., "is this feature needed?", "which approach do you prefer?")
- `not_found` → exhausted search avenues, nothing relevant found

clarify.prompt:
Findings so far require user input before proceeding.

Present what you've found so far concisely, then ask your question(s).
Use AskUserQuestion for critical decisions that affect the direction of exploration.

If there is no interactive user (you are running as a subagent), do NOT
ask — state your assumptions and continue, or take the failure path.

After getting user's answer → transition `continue` to resume investigation
with the new context, or `enough` if the answer completes the picture.

synthesize.prompt:
Compile findings into a structured answer.

Format:
- Start with a concise summary (1-2 sentences)
- Key files and their roles
- Architecture/patterns discovered
- Code flow if traced

If this reveals a recurring knowledge gap → note it for reflection.

When the synthesis is presented → transition `done`. If the findings
indicate code changes, say so in the synthesis — the parent workflow
decides what happens next.

self_review.prompt:
Re-read what you just wrote. Code review only — do NOT build or run tests.

You are reviewing ONE file or a small COUPLED BATCH as part of a code
review. The file list, why the files are grouped, and diff info come
from your task prompt (spawned agent) or from the conversation so far
(inline sub-workflow). Every "this file" below means "each file in
your batch"; read the batch's shared context (imports, siblings) once,
and also check the seams the grouping names (caller↔callee, test↔source).

1. Read the diff for this file to understand what changed.
2. Check the review scope from your task prompt:
   - `diff` scope → read the diff, then read the full methods/blocks containing changes.
     Changes can affect surrounding code, so always understand the logical context.
   - `full` scope → read the FULL file
3. Read related files: imports, files that call this one, siblings in the same module.

4. Understand what changed and why.

   `context_set(key: "file_path", value: "<ABSOLUTE path(s), space-separated>")`
6. hxq availability (engine probe): "{{context.hxq_available}}" (empty = unavailable).

Then → transition `done`.

determine_authorship.prompt:
Decide whether this file is user-authored or external/forked/vendored —
this gates which personal rules apply downstream (style + architecture).

Strong signals it is external / forked / vendored (set "false"):
- `git remote -v` points to a third-party upstream the user does not control.
- README/CLAUDE.md mentions "fork of X", "based on X", "vendored from X".
- Path lives under `node_modules/`, `vendor/`, `third_party/`, a haxelib
  cache, or similar dependency location.

Save the verdict:
- ANY strong external signal present → `context_set({ key: "is_user_authored", value: "false" })`
- Otherwise → `context_set({ key: "is_user_authored", value: "true" })`

Default to "true" when signals are ambiguous — external markers are reliably
detectable; user-authored markers are not, so ambiguity falls on the
personal-rules side. Do not block on user input.

Then → transition `done`.

build_checklist.prompt:
**Step 1 — mechanical-pass verdict (run this whatever the authorship —
the linter's report is about the code, not about who wrote it).**
The engine already ran the project linter on this file; its report:
---
{{context.lint_report}}
---
Decide ONCE what the linter verified, and record it for the
downstream states — they read these two keys and never re-derive them:
- USABLE = non-empty, the `=== hxq lint` / `=== fmt drift` headers name
  THIS batch's files, and so do the `file:` lines under each
  `=== effective lint rules` block (other files anywhere = stale report
  from an earlier pass in a reused session), and the lint section is
  real output — not "SKIP: ..." and not a mid-report "SKIP: hxq lint
  failed" (a broken linter verified nothing). Per-file SKIP lines for
  the batch's non-.hx files are normal — the report is usable for the
  .hx files it covers; but a report with NO `===` lint section at all
  (only SKIP lines) is NOT usable.
- NOT usable → `context_set(key: "lint_subtraction", value: "none")`
  and `context_set(key: "lint_rules_ran", value: "")`.
- USABLE → its findings are review facts: carry them into your report
  as-is, whatever the rule-state section says. Then read that section:
  - `=== hxq lint rules: effective state per file` → one block per
    config chain, each listing its `file:` lines and then
    `<rule-id>  on|off  <reason>  <description>` per rule. A rule
    counts as RAN only if it is `on` in the block of EVERY batch .hx
    file (a rule on for some files only stays manual for the whole
    batch). Record them:
    `context_set(key: "lint_rules_ran", value: "<comma-separated ids>")`
    and `context_set(key: "lint_subtraction", value: "applied")`.
    `off` rules — config-disabled, `default-off` (opt-in, never
    enabled), `needs-language-<v>`, `needs-config` / `config-excluded`
    / `config-noop` (the rule's own options skip that file) — did NOT
    run: never subtract them. A batch file carrying a
    `// CHECKSTYLE:OFF` region had its findings there suppressed, so
    nothing was verified for that code: subtract nothing for that file
    (a `// noqa` line likewise leaves that line to you).
  - `=== hxq lint rules: registry only` (hxq too old to report the
    effective state), `=== hxq lint rules: unavailable`, a SKIP there,
    or no rule-state section at all → the linter's coverage is
    unknown: subtract nothing. Record
    `context_set(key: "lint_rules_ran", value: "")` and
    `context_set(key: "lint_subtraction", value: "none")`.

**Step 2 — authorship gate.** Check `{{context.is_user_authored}}`.
Treat empty as `"true"` (default).
If `"false"` → personal style rules do not apply. Output:
"Skipping personal-style checklist — file is external/forked/vendored.
check_style will use only language-agnostic checks."
Then → transition `done` (the Step 1 verdict still stands: downstream
states subtract by it for their language-agnostic checks).

**Step 3 — build the checklist out of what is LEFT.**
Process the bare `preferences` skill plus each loaded `lang-*` and
`preferences-*` skill ONE AT A TIME.
For each skill:
1. Re-read the FULL skill text
2. For EVERY rule in it — each `// WRONG` example, explicit rule, or
   convention:
   - subtraction "applied" AND a rule in `lint_rules_ran` covers it →
     DROP it, write no check line. Subtract at rule granularity: a rule
     covers exactly what its description says, no more.
   - otherwise → one line with the wrong pattern AND the correct one
3. Output this skill's kept count and dropped count

Do NOT summarize, group, or prioritize — every kept rule matters equally.
Rules no linter can verify always stay: comment quality, abstraction
threshold, naming semantics, API shape, domain correctness.

With subtraction "none" nothing is dropped — and if your total is then
under 25 rules across all skills, you missed some: re-read.

Escape hatch: if NO lang/preferences skills apply to this file type
(e.g. config, YAML, docs), state so explicitly and continue — the
language-agnostic checks in the following states still run.

Output the full checklist, then → transition `done`.

check_correctness.prompt:
Check based on review scope (`diff` or `full`).
For `diff` scope: changed lines are entry points, but always check the
logical context around them — the full method, callers of changed signatures,
other uses of changed fields. A change can break surrounding code.

If `{{context.lint_subtraction}}` is "applied", the linter ran exactly
these rules: `{{context.lint_rules_ran}}` — their findings are in the
report. Do not re-derive by hand what THOSE rules cover (e.g.
`null-dereference`, `dead-null-guard`, `swallowed-exception`,
`dead-code`, `identical-operands`, `assignment-in-condition` — each only
if it is in that list). Anything not in the list is still yours.
Your job here is the part no linter can prove: whether the logic is
what the change INTENDED.

- [ ] Logic errors: wrong conditions, off-by-one, inverted booleans, wrong operators
- [ ] Dead guards: for EVERY guard/early-return/conditional check in changed code,
      trace all call sites and ask "can this condition ever be true/false here?"
      Apply knowledge from loaded skills (e.g. library callback ordering, lifecycle
      guarantees). If no execution path triggers the guard — it's dead code, remove it.
- [ ] Edge cases: null/undefined, empty collections, zero, negative, boundary values
- [ ] Error handling: uncaught exceptions, swallowed errors, wrong error types
- [ ] Race conditions: async without awaits, shared mutable state
- [ ] Resource leaks: unclosed handles, missing cleanup in error paths
- [ ] Type mismatches: wrong argument types, unsafe casts
- [ ] Regression risk: does this break existing callers or assumptions?

Then → transition `done`.

check_loops.prompt:
Find loops based on review scope (`diff` = only loops in changed code, `full` = ALL loops in file). For each one, output:

  Line <N>: `<the loop header>` — iterates <what> to access <what> → verdict: ok / issue

Check each loop against these anti-patterns. The examples are
Haxe-flavored — translate each pattern to the file's language.
Rules 5-6 are personal style preferences — apply them ONLY when
`{{context.is_user_authored}}` is not "false" (treat empty as "true");
for external/forked/vendored code check rules 1-4 only.
If `{{context.lint_subtraction}}` is "applied", skip a rule below ONLY
when its counterpart rule id is in `{{context.lint_rules_ran}}`: 2 ↔
`map-keys-lookup`, 5 ↔ `loop-guard`, 6 ↔ `prefer-switch`. Rules 1, 3
and 4 are pure judgment, owned by no linter — walk EVERY loop for those.

1. **Range-over-sparse-container**: the loop iterates an index range (`0...n`,
   `i++`) but uses the index to look up a Map/Dict/HashMap, with a null check
   to skip missing entries. This means the container is sparse and should be
   iterated directly instead of via index range.
   WRONG: `for (i in 0...n) { val = map[i]; if (val == null) continue; ... }`
   RIGHT: `for (key => val in map) { ... }` (with filter if needed)

2. **Keys-then-lookup**: iterates `.keys()` then does a separate `map[key]`
   lookup inside the body. Use key-value destructuring instead.
   WRONG: `for (k in map.keys()) { v = map[k]; ... }`
   RIGHT: `for (k => v in map) { ... }`

3. **Repeated linear scan**: the same collection is scanned multiple times in
   the same method or call chain to find related data that could be found in
   a single pass.

4. **Wrong container for access pattern**: Array with `.contains()` checks
   (should be Set/Map), unsorted Array with binary-search-like access, etc.

5. **Continue instead of guard**: when a single condition filters the entire
   loop body, use guard-style `for (...) if (cond) {` instead of
   `if (!cond) continue;`. But when multiple independent checks follow
   sequentially (each with its own variable), `continue` is fine.
   WRONG: `for (x in list) { if (x.type != Foo) continue; doWork(x); }`
   RIGHT: `for (x in list) if (x.type == Foo) { doWork(x); }`
   OK:    `for (f in range) { val = map[f]; if (val == null) continue; ... }`

6. **If/else-if chain instead of switch**: when a loop body checks the same
   variable with `if/else if` chain (e.g. `if (x == "a") ... else if (x == "b")`),
   use `switch` instead — cleaner, exhaustive, idiomatic.
   WRONG: `if (node.name == "a") { ... } else if (node.name == "b") { ... }`
   RIGHT: `switch node.name { case "a": ... case "b": ... }`

You MUST list ALL loops with verdicts. Do not summarize or skip "obvious" ones.

Then → transition `done`.
check_loops.task: Audit every loop and iteration pattern

check_style.prompt:
Authorship: `{{context.is_user_authored}}` (set in determine_authorship).
Treat empty as `"true"` (default).

If `"false"` (external / forked / vendored):
Skip the personal-style checklist entirely. Match THAT codebase's existing
style — a one-line patch into a foreign project should look like it belongs.
Only flag issues from the language-agnostic checks below.

Otherwise (user-authored):
Go through EVERY item in your style checklist from build_checklist.
Personal rules are authoritative — a neighboring file violating the same
rule is a bug replicated in both places, not a valid pattern. Flag it.
Never dismiss a checklist hit with "the sibling does it this way".

Scope: `diff` = scan only lines in the diff; `full` = scan entire file.
If a line appears in the diff, it is part of the change and must meet
current style standards. Report with file:line.

If `{{context.lint_subtraction}}` is "applied", skip the parts of the
items below that a rule in `{{context.lint_rules_ran}}` already
verified and hand-check only the residues those rules' descriptions
do not cover — e.g. "function doing too many things" beyond the
cyclomatic threshold, semantics of names (the `naming` rule checks the
convention, not whether the name says the right thing), commented-out
code, consistency judgments against this module's patterns.

Language-agnostic checks (apply regardless of authorship):
- [ ] Missing type annotations: if a variable/field/parameter has no explicit type
      and adding one would improve clarity, recommend it — but ONLY after you find
      the actual type definition in the codebase (via Grep/Read). Never guess types.
      Use short type names + import, not fully qualified paths (e.g. `MyClass`,
      not `com.package.MyClass`) — unless a name conflict or conditional compilation
      requires the full path (check loaded lang/preferences skills for specifics).
- [ ] Naming: consistent with the conventions of THIS codebase (the user's own
      for user-authored, the upstream's for external).
- [ ] Member ordering: new fields and methods must respect class member order
      (constants → public vars → private vars → constructor → instance methods →
      static methods). Check that added code is in the right section, not just
      appended next to related code.
- [ ] Duplication: does this duplicate existing code? Search the codebase.
- [ ] Dead code: unused imports, commented-out code (dead guards checked in check_correctness).
      Imports used only inside conditional-compilation blocks are dead in
      the other branches — reference such symbols via fully qualified name
      inside the conditional block instead of adding a top-level import.
- [ ] Complexity: overly nested logic, functions doing too many things
- [ ] Consistency: does new code follow patterns in the same module of THIS
      codebase? (For user-authored code, this means the user's own conventions —
      not a license to replicate violations from sibling files.)

Then → transition `done`.

check_architecture.prompt:
Authorship: `{{context.is_user_authored}}` (set in determine_authorship).
Treat empty as `"true"` (default).

Check structural quality (scope: `diff` = changed code, `full` = entire file).

Language-agnostic checks (apply regardless of authorship):
- [ ] Unnecessary indirection: wrapper classes/methods that just forward calls
- [ ] Dead abstractions: interface with one implementation, base class with one subclass
- [ ] God class: file doing too many unrelated things — should it be split?
- [ ] Overcomplicated: deep inheritance or nesting that could be flattened
- [ ] Wrong level: logic placed in the wrong layer (UI doing data work, model doing display)
- [ ] Stale patterns: old patterns that predate current codebase conventions
- [ ] Complexity without pain: abstractions, patterns, or layers added for hypothetical future needs

Architecture-skill checks (skip ONLY when `is_user_authored` is `"false"`):
- [ ] Initialization in parent: parent manually triggers component's internal setup — should be inside the component
- [ ] Serialization in runtime state: serialize/deserialize mixed into state classes — should be separate
- [ ] Event re-dispatch duplication: re-dispatched event carries fields that duplicate event.target

Only flag real simplification opportunities — don't invent hypothetical improvements.

Then → transition `done`.

check_security.prompt:
Check code for security issues (scope: `diff` = changed code, `full` = entire file):
- [ ] Injection: unsanitized inputs reaching dangerous APIs
- [ ] Auth/authz: missing or insufficient access controls
- [ ] Data exposure: secrets, credentials, or sensitive data leaking
- [ ] Input validation: missing validation at system boundaries
- [ ] Unsafe operations: anything exploitable by malicious input

Only flag real risks — don't invent hypothetical issues.
Then → transition `done`.

report.prompt:
Write a structured report — ONE section per batch file, then (for a
multi-file batch) a closing **Cross-file** section for findings on the
seams between them. Per file:

**File**: <path>
**What changed**: <one-paragraph summary of the changes>
**Issues found**:
For each issue:
- Severity: bug / risk / style / nit / pre-existing
  (`pre-existing` = issue outside the changed lines, found during
  a diff-scope review — report separately, do NOT mix with diff issues)
- Line: <line number>
- Description: <what's wrong>
- Suggestion: <how to fix>

If no issues found, say so explicitly.

Output this report — as your final response (spawned agent) or into the
conversation for the parent workflow (inline sub-workflow).
Then → transition `done`.

github-init.description: Initialize git repo and create a private GitHub repository for a project not yet on GitHub

check_state.prompt:
Check the current state of the project:
1. `git status` — is it already a git repo?
2. `gh auth status` — is GitHub CLI authenticated?
3. `git remote -v` — is a GitHub remote already configured?
4. Check if `.gitignore` exists

Choose transition:
- `needs_gitignore` → not a git repo, no .gitignore
- `needs_init` → .gitignore exists but not a git repo
- `needs_repo` → already a git repo, just needs GitHub remote
- `already_done` → git repo with GitHub remote already set — just verify

enqueue_plan.prompt:
Hand the approved plan's tasks to the task queue; do NOT implement anything here.

1. **Read** the plan's `## Tasks` table and the steps under each task, and check EVERY task
   before the first `queue_add` (a pass is all-or-nothing; see 4):
   - every `touches` path exists (`git ls-files`, `ls`) or is a new file under an existing
     directory. If ANY path of a task fails, remove that task's WHOLE `touches` list: a list
     with a path missing claims less than the task edits and lets it run beside a task on that
     path, while no `touches` makes it run alone in its repo (slower, never wrong). Then check
     overlap on what remains: two tasks without an `after` between them whose paths overlap
     → add the `after` (dependencies first).
   - each task stands alone (testable, reviewable, landable, main green). A task that cannot
     → fold it into the task it depends on as steps. `after` ids exist and form no cycle.
   `touches` is a claim the land does not verify. `project_land` is `git merge --no-ff` plus
   `land_test`: it stops on a textual conflict or a red test, and two tasks that edited
   different hunks of an undeclared shared file merge cleanly. The seams between tasks are
   what `batch`'s `cross_check` of the combined diff reads.
2. **Which queue.** A project heir of `batch` = a workflow file with `extends: batch` in
   `<project>/.claude/workflows/` (also `~/.claude/workflows/`): `grep -lE '^extends: *batch *$'`
   (anchored: `extends: batch-task` is a task-workflow heir with no `plan_queue`, not a queue heir) —
   the list printed below carries names and descriptions only, never `extends`. Heir found →
   read its `plan_queue` for the queue it names; that queue may be live and fixed, so
   `queue_add` into it (`file:`/`queue:` as it names) and leave its header (`batch_size`,
   `reason`) and `queue_file` alone; set context `project_workflow` to the heir and transition
   `project`. The heir's queue cannot be read → tell the user and transition `replan`. No heir
   → the bundled `batch` with this plan's own queue `plan-<slug>` (a short slug of the plan's
   topic) and transition `batch`.
3. The queue file must stay out of git: `git check-ignore -q .claude/batch/` else append
   `.claude/batch/` to the file `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` prints (local only,
   right in a linked worktree; a tracked queue dirties the tree and every land refuses).
4. **`queue_add`** one line per task, dependencies first: `{id, status: pending, difficulty,
   after, touches, text}`. `text` is SELF-CONTAINED — the goal, the steps numbered, the
   constraints and how to tell it is done: the worker sees only its line, never this plan. Ids
   as in the plan; if an id is already in the queue and is not this plan's task, prefix all of
   this plan's ids with the slug and rewrite `after`. The first add creates the queue. A task
   whose id is already in the queue from THIS plan (a retry after an interrupted pass) is
   skipped, never duplicated. A refused add → fix the line (`queue_edit`) and retry. Unfixable
   after earlier adds of this pass → `queue_edit` each of this pass's lines to `parked: true`
   (a pick skips a parked line; a live heir queue must never admit half a plan), then tell the
   user and transition `replan`; the revised plan queues under new ids.
5. Own queue only (`plan-<slug>`): `queue_header({queue, batch_size: N, reason: "plan:
   <slug>"})` — N = the tasks with no `after`, at most 3 — and `context_set(key: "queue_file",
   value: "<absolute path of the queue file>")` (the add's answer names it). `batch`'s
   `plan_queue` finishes the header (`base:`, `land_test:`) and resumes this queue. A heir's
   queue: no header write.

design.prompt:
Design the implementation plan. (Coding skills incl. architecture
and the project's structural-navigation skill were loaded at the
`load_skills` gate — follow them; do not default to grep on
parseable source.)

**Plan mode**: if system prompt says "Plan mode is active" — you're already in it,
do NOT call EnterPlanMode. Otherwise call `EnterPlanMode`.

**Dynamic check**: If the task is operational/multi-step (not pure code changes —
e.g. git operations, deployment, file management, CI/CD setup) → transition `dynamic`
to create the execution workflow directly instead of writing a text plan.

**Data flow rule**: when the task involves reading or writing persistent data
(files, cache, database), the explore phase MUST trace the complete data flow:
write → serialize → load → copy → consumer. Don't stop at 'found where it's
stored' — follow the path until you see how the data reaches its consumers.
Check how analogous fields in the same system are handled.

**Before proposing a new storage mechanism** (Store, DB column, file scan):
verify — does the project already have infrastructure for this type of data?
Check how similar fields are stored and propagated. Use existing infrastructure first.

**UI animation plans**: for any animation/transition changes, include a
per-element table: Element | Start state | End state | Tween props | Notes.
Ambiguous phrases like "crossfade" or "morph" cause misinterpretation.
Be explicit: "icon tweens x from 0 to -offset, alpha 1→0, no y change."

**Plan scope**: focus on WHAT to change and WHY. Do NOT include build, run,
or launch steps in the plan — the execution workflow handles building and
running automatically in its review/testing states. Including them causes
the agent to run manual builds that conflict with the automated pipeline.

**Tasks and steps** (two levels, both in the plan). A TASK can be tested, reviewed
and landed on its own and leaves main green. A STEP cannot, or is too small to pay
for its own check, review and land: it shares its task's. Split into tasks only
along that line: work that compiles or passes only together is ONE task with
steps; a change that is useful without the rest is its own task. A small change
written in several places is one task with steps, not a queue.
- One task (any number of steps): write the steps; no table.
- Two or more tasks: add a `## Tasks` table and the steps under each task:
  ```
  ## Tasks
  | id | after | touches | difficulty |
  |----|-------|---------|------------|
  | T1 | —     | src/a, docs/x.md | 4 |
  | T2 | T1    | src/b            | 3 |

  ### T1 — <title>
  1. <step>
  2. <step>
  ```
  `after` = tasks that must land first (an order the code needs, not a wish);
  `touches` = paths (prefixes) the task edits — check each exists (or is a new
  file under an existing directory) before naming it; if any path of a task
  cannot be checked, the task gets no `touches` at all (it then runs alone, which is
  slow but never wrong; a partial list claims less than the task edits);
  `difficulty` per the rubric (1..10). Two tasks with no `after` between
  them must not share a path.

**Brevity**: fewer steps. Skip what the user can infer from the task. Don't
restate the task back at the top of the plan. No filler sections (`Overview`,
`Background`) unless the task is genuinely novel and context is needed.

**Steps in plan mode:**
1. Explore codebase (directly or via Plan/Explore subagents — explicit
   `model` + `effort`: `haiku`/low to locate, `opus`/high for design-critical analysis)
2. Design approach — the PLAN itself is built HERE, inline, never in a
   plan sub-agent: it condenses the user dialog no brief can carry,
   and the planner must be the dispatcher (recon delegates, the plan
   does not)
3. Write plan to the plan file specified in plan mode system prompt
4. Plan file MUST end with Workflow section (get session_id via `status`):
   ```
   ## Workflow
   - **Session**: `<session_id>`
   - **Current state**: `planning @ design`
   - **After approve**: transition `planned` → returns to parent
   - **Execution workflow**: coding / docs / feature / bug_fix / testing / refactoring / <workflow-name>; `batch` when there are two or more tasks
   - **Resume**: `transition("<session_id>", "planned")`
   - **Tasks**: <N> (1 = one task, its steps run in the Execution workflow; 2 or more = the `## Tasks` table is queued and run by `batch`)
   ```
   Keep `Tasks` the LAST line, after Resume: the start hook reads the section by
   position (Session within five lines of the heading).
5. Call `ExitPlanMode` for user approval

**After plan approved → transition `planned`.**
**If the user rejects the plan** → revise the plan file per their feedback,
then call `ExitPlanMode` again. Do NOT transition until approved.
